event.asset: midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD: FDA treatment of the Phase 3 double-blind in its review of the application

event.proposition: The FDA's written action on, or review of, the midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) application for post-traumatic stress disorder cites an unsuccessful double-blind (functional unblinding) in the Phase 3 trials as a basis for not accepting the efficacy results.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of an FDA written action (complete response letter, refuse-to-file letter or other written communication that the sponsor discloses), an FDA review document posted on Drugs@FDA, or an FDA advisory committee briefing document that names failure or loss of the double-blind (functional unblinding, expectancy bias from unblinding) in the Phase 3 trials of midomafetamine for PTSD as a reason the efficacy results are not adequate for approval. A published FDA document that only asks a question about blinding without treating it as a deficiency does not count. FALSE if the FDA approves the application without such a finding, or if no such document exists at the deadline. Resolution source: Drugs@FDA (action letters and review documents) and the FDA advisory committee materials page, with the sponsor's disclosure of the letter as a secondary source.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA (action letters, review documents) and FDA advisory committee materials; sponsor disclosure of the letter as a secondary source

readings: 'Our final results will not be challenged on the basis of an unsuccessful double-blind' = the FDA does not cite unblinding as a deficiency of the Phase 3 efficacy results; the forecaster denies the proposition.
Any sponsor name (MAPS PBC, Lykos Therapeutics or a successor) counts; the entry is on the asset.
Distinct from E-0027 (safety data cited in a non-approval) and from E-0001 (approval): this event is about the stated basis of the FDA's assessment, not the approval decision.

records.phrase: we know that our final results will not be challenged on the basis of an unsuccessful double-blind
records.stage_note: On 2017-09-05 the program was between the FDA Special Protocol Assessment agreement (July 2017) and the first Phase 3 site opening. No class in base-rates.json covers the content of an FDA review finding, so base_rate_class is null.
records.note: A forecast of FDA conduct: the FDA will not reject the Phase 3 results on the ground that the double-blind failed. The FDA decides what its review cites, so a third party decides; affiliated because MAPS PBC is the sponsor and the forecaster is founder and president of MAPS. 'Will not' denies the event: per the prompt, a denial takes bin A with asserts false ('the FDA will not approve X' pattern); tag denial. 'We know that' is a certainty marker consistent with A. No date in the words, so undated (24-month window). Not KNOWN: no Phase 3 result or FDA review existed on the statement date. A coder who reads the sentence as a description of the SPA letter rather than an expectation would reject NOT_FORECAST; the words are future tense about the FDA's future action, so this coder admits.

The sentences state what FDA approval 'depends on' and 'relies on' (fundraising of $25 million, of which $12.5 million raised; 80 co-therapists at over a dozen sites): a list of dependencies and a status report, not an assertion that a future state occurs. The approval forecast itself is the next sentence, already in the census as doblin-0001. Alternative code CONTROL (own fundraising and own site roll-out) is secondary because no outcome is asserted at all.

The cost of the forecaster's own program ('$26 million we currently estimate we will need for FDA approval', and that the same sum 'may also be sufficient' for EMA) is MAPS's own spending, set by its own budget decisions; the amount raised ('more than $18 million') is a status report. No public series defines 'the cost of FDA approval' for a non-profit sponsor, so the alternative code is VAGUE; CONTROL is primary because the outcome is the organization's own expenditure.

Both halves are actions of the forecaster's own organization: initiating 'the first Phase 3 study' in H1 2018 is a trial start, and 'submitting our New Drug Application to the FDA in 2021' is a filing; both are in the CONTROL list. Not split: neither half is admissible (same treatment as doblin-0004).

The timing of the interim analysis of 'our first Phase 3 study' (near the beginning of 2019) is set by the sponsor's own enrolment and protocol schedule; a trial milestone of the forecaster's own organization. The sample-size outcome of the analysis is not forecast ('we won't know how many subjects we are going to need').

MAPS's own expense projections for FY18 ($8,397,560) and FY19 (over $12 million) are budget decisions of the forecaster's organization. A public series exists (MAPS Form 990 and audited financials), but spending is made to happen by the organization's own decision, so CONTROL rather than a quantity event.

Completing Phase 3 data gathering in FY20 and submitting an NDA in FY21 are the forecaster's own organization's trial completion and filing; the expense trajectory is its own budget. All in the CONTROL list; not split.

'MAPS is seeking to raise these funds by the end of February 2018' states a fundraising goal, not an expectation that the $8 million arrives; the cost estimate ('$26 million is needed') is the organization's own budget (CONTROL, as in doblin-0059). No future state is asserted, so NOT_FORECAST is primary. Donations are decided by donors, so a coder who reads 'seeking to' as an expectation could write a quantity event on MAPS's own reported receipts, but no independent series reports them.

'Income from the sales of MDMA ... can supplement and potentially even replace the need for philanthropic donations' 'over time': no threshold, no ratio, no named series and no deadline ('over time' is not an anchor pattern). The first half (MPBC 'can begin the sale of medical grade MDMA by prescription' once approved) is a capability statement about the forecaster's own organization's product launch (CONTROL). The condition (FDA approval) is observable, but the consequent cannot be resolved.

'We will begin discussions with FDA' in FY18 is an action of the forecaster's own organization (requesting and holding meetings under its Breakthrough Therapy Designation). No FDA decision is forecast.

No expectation verb and no date. Alternative reading: a conditional forecast, E-0001 conditional on E-0002 (MAPP1 primary endpoint met) with bin A on 'commitment', undated; this coder does not adopt it because the words report the letter's content, and the forecaster's own approval forecasts appear elsewhere in the same column with dates.

Training of the forecaster's own Phase 3 therapists by Fall 2018, Phase 3 starting at 'most of our sites this August' and the trials 'taking roughly two years to complete' are trial start and trial completion timing of the forecaster's own organization. Not split.

Raising $5 million, beginning Phase 3 in Europe in summer 2019 and completing it in 12 to 16 months are fundraising, trial start and trial completion by the forecaster's own organization. 'Coming to agreement with EMA before the end of this year' is the close of the sponsor's own scientific-advice negotiation: the sponsor can accept whatever Phase 3 requirements EMA sets, so it can make the agreement happen, and no EMA database records the agreement. A coder who reads the EMA half as a regulator's decision could write a rule_or_policy event on EMA scientific advice with deadline 2018-12-31 and bin B ('anticipate'); this coder keeps CONTROL for the whole compound.

The end of the federal monopoly on DEA-licensed research cannabis (DEA registering additional bulk manufacturers) is a drug-supply licensing decision for all FDA-regulated cannabis research, not an approval, scheduling or rule-making decision about a drug, device or treatment in psychiatry; MAPS's PTSD study is one user of that supply, which does not make the DEA licensing decision a psychiatric regulatory event. If it were in area, 'feels likely to be a successful conclusion' would be bin B, undated ('approaching' is not an anchor pattern), and the event would be a rule_or_policy entry on DEA granting at least one additional cannabis manufacturer registration.

Same asset as doblin-0072 (DEA action on cannabis cultivation licences), so the same area failure. 'Actions rather than just words' also names no specific DEA act, and 'soon' is not a deadline, so VAGUE is the secondary code.

'A supply of cannabis that could ultimately be sold as a prescription medicine': no indication, no regulator named for the prescription approval, no sponsor product, and 'ultimately' is not a deadline. MAPS's own access to a supply (the first clause) is its own action. The condition (end of the federal monopoly) is observable but the consequent cannot be written as an event without inventing the indication and the regulator.

Class phase3_to_approval_psychiatry (p 0.563, median 36 months) is the nearest fit; no class in the table is specific to Health Canada or to approval after a prior FDA approval. The 24-month undated window is below the median, so b is halved.
records.note: Half b of the compound: Canada. Conditional on FDA approval: condition E-0001, tag conditional. Health Canada decides, so a third party decides; affiliated because MAPS PBC is the sponsor. 'Will also become approved' sets bin A; asserts true. No date in the words, so undated.

event.asset: midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD: FDA labeling or REMS restriction of administration to therapists trained through the sponsor's program
event.title: FDA restricts midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) administration to sponsor-trained therapists
event.proposition: The FDA approves midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for post-traumatic stress disorder with labeling or a REMS under which only therapists who have completed the sponsor's (MAPS) training program may administer the treatment.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of an FDA approval of midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD, under any sponsor name, whose approved labeling or REMS document (REMS@FDA) requires that the therapists or healthcare providers who administer or monitor dosing sessions complete a training or certification program provided or certified by the sponsor (MAPS, MAPS PBC, Lykos Therapeutics or a successor), with no other route to eligibility. FALSE on the date of an approval whose labeling and REMS permit administration by providers without sponsor-provided training, or set no provider training requirement. Unresolved while no approval exists. Resolution source: Drugs@FDA (approved labeling) and REMS@FDA.
readings: 'The only therapists who will be able to directly administer it ... are going to be therapists that have been through our training program' (doblin-0088) and 'MAPS will be the only FDA-approved entity to train therapists for MDMA-assisted therapy' (doblin-0094) name the same restriction.
A REMS whose certification program is run by the sponsor or by a training body it designates counts; a REMS that accepts training from any accredited provider does not.
Distinct from new:fda-midomafetamine-ptsd-rems-at-approval (any REMS) and from new:fda-midomafetamine-ptsd-supervised-clinic-only (setting restriction).

records.phrase: MAPS will be the only FDA-approved entity to train therapists for MDMA-assisted therapy
records.stage_note: On 2019-09-10 the Phase 3 program was enrolling; no NDA. No class in base-rates.json covers labeling or REMS content, so base_rate_class is null.
records.note: Split of a compound (training exclusivity 'and' clinic count): half a is 'MAPS will be the only FDA-approved entity to train therapists for MDMA-assisted therapy', the same restriction as doblin-0088-a, so it maps to the event proposed there (new:fda-midomafetamine-ptsd-sponsor-trained-therapists-only, full proposal in doblin-0088-a). The FDA decides the labeling and REMS, so a third party decides; affiliated because MAPS is the training body and MAPS PBC the sponsor. 'Will be' sets bin A; asserts true. The answer presupposes FDA approval but states no condition, so no conditional tag; the event itself resolves only at approval. No date, undated. Q&A in the forecaster's own words.

Half b: 'There will be 10,000 clinics in America eventually.' The threshold is numeric, but no named series counts clinics that administer MDMA-assisted therapy (or psychedelic clinics) in the United States, the set is undefined (ketamine clinics existed in 2019), and 'eventually' is not a deadline (anchors.json). Same failure as doblin-0008. 'Once the therapists have been trained, they can set up their own clinics' is a capability statement.

'They'll probably just wait this out': a denial that any other sponsor generates its own MDMA data and markets a competing product during the five-year data-exclusivity window. The window starts at an FDA approval with no date in these words, so no deadline can be set; 'more than five years and $35 million or $40 million' is the cost to a competitor, not a horizon; and 'wait this out' does not say whether the competitor files nothing, files after exclusivity, or files a generic on MAPS's data. A coder could write a company_event on Drugs@FDA (a second sponsor's MDMA NDA supported by its own trials before the first approval's exclusivity ends, asserts false, bin B), but the deadline would have to be invented from a future approval date, so this coder rejects VAGUE.
